title: An object can do a job
hook: How an object is used matters to the description.

knows: Animals can respond to cues and conditions.
doesNotKnow: In a toy observation, animal A moves a stick aside; animal B uses a stick to pull food within reach. Which action is an example of tool use under this stated definition?

misconception: The stated evidence implies a different interpretation or a universal conclusion.
objective: In a toy observation, animal A moves a stick aside; animal B uses a stick to pull food within reach. Which action is an example of tool use under this stated definition?

claims.text: In a toy observation, animal A moves a stick aside; animal B uses a stick to pull food within reach. Which action is an example of tool use under this stated definition? In panel A, the stick is moved aside. In panel B, the stick helps bring food within reach. Under this lesson’s operational definition, the second action is tool use; a real study would need sufficient evidence about how the object is used.

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative model and do not depict observed data.
An animal uses a twig to pull an out-of-reach item closer. Under the stated definition, what is the twig doing? The twig serves a role in reaching the item under the stated definition.
